name: Shahed-136 / Geran-2
representative_system: Shahed-136 / Geran-2 — Long-range one-way attack drone

image.license: See Commons file page for license

cost.display: $20,000-70,000 depending on source and production generation (domestic Russian production estimated higher than original Iranian export cost)

key_facts.label: Warhead
key_facts.value: 50kg warhead (up to 90kg in later Russian variants)

characteristics: 50kg warhead (up to 90kg in later Russian variants)
GNSS/INS guidance, no seeker in baseline configuration
Strength: Very long range and low cost per unit enable mass 'saturation' raids that overwhelm air defense economically, not just numerically
Limitation: No optical seeker in the baseline version - it can only strike pre-programmed fixed coordinates, not moving or newly-appearing targets
Estimated quantity available: Mass produced at the Alabuga facility in Tatarstan; production rate estimated in the hundreds to low thousands per month by mid-2020s reporting
employment_notes: The single clearest embodiment of the cost-asymmetry problem discussed throughout the doctrine reference: a ~$20-50K drone forcing the use of $400K-$5M interceptors to shoot it down
contrast_vs_traditional: Long-range one-way attack drones invert the traditional cost logic of deep strike — where a cruise missile or manned bomber sortie once carried a cost per strike in the hundreds of thousands to millions of dollars, mass-produced Shahed/Geran strikes trade precision and survivability for sheer volume, saturating air defense economically rather than penetrating it technically.

sources.label: Covert Shores (H I Sutton) — Guide to Russian Shahed/Geran strike drones

notes: Specs meet the bar but the unit cost is an estimate — cost is not verified.
